_README: A worked example of a role profile deliberately unlike the one in the eval fixtures — different function, different stack, different geography. It exists to show that the scripts carry no assumptions: swap this file for another and the same scrapers issue entirely different queries.
context: Series-B B2B SaaS, 40 people. The nightly pipeline misses its SLA three days a week and nobody owns the warehouse. This hire owns ingestion through serving.
abar_legs: L1 Has personally owned a production data platform end to end: ingestion, orchestration, warehouse modelling, and serving. Named system + a public artefact (talk, post, repo, or docs).
L2 Has run a pipeline with a real SLA and been on the hook when it broke — evidence of incident ownership, not just authorship.
L3 Scale evidence: a stated volume (events/day, TB, or table count) they were responsible for.
L4 NYC-based or EU-remote-eligible with stated work authorization.
L5 At least 2 distinct public evidence URLs, all resolving.
exclude: ML engineers with no platform ownership
consultants with no named production system
evidence only behind a login wall
